title: How many passcodes can the digital locker have?
description: A digital locker uses a passcode of five slots, and each slot can hold a letter or a digit. The video counts the choices for one slot and multiplies them slot by slot, the same way as the letter lock.
teaching_notes: One idea: when each slot has the same number of choices, the passcodes are that number multiplied by itself once for each slot. Watch for students who count twenty six letters and ten digits separately and multiply them, or who add them once for the whole passcode.

video_script.why: A learner uses the choices-for-each-slot method of the letter lock on a slot that can hold a letter or a digit.
video_script.substitution: the book's own digital locker with a passcode of five slots
video_script.anchor: the digital locker with five passcode slots
video_script.payoff_line: Five slots of thirty six choices make thirty six to the power five passcodes

final_answer.value: 36 to the power 5, which is 60466176 codes
final_answer.spoken: thirty six to the power five, which is six crore four lakh sixty six thousand one hundred and seventy six codes

maths_rules: 26 letters + 10 digits = 36 choices for each slot
6 x 6 = 36 ends in 6, so every power of 36 ends in 6
video_script.design: One idea: choices for each slot, multiplied once for each slot. The locker keeps its five slots on the board and the total only appears at the answer.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; a digital locker with 5 slots; example codes G89P0, 38098, BRJKW and 003AZ

marks.locker: the digital locker appears with five empty slots
marks.codes: the example codes G89P0, 38098, BRJKW and 003AZ fill the slots one after another
marks.ask: a question mark glows over the locker

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This question is from your book.
<bookmark mark='locker'/>A digital locker has a passcode of five slots.
<bookmark mark='codes'/>A slot can hold a letter or a digit. Some codes use both, and some use only one kind.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How many such passcodes are possible?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: one slot showing the 26 letters and the 10 digits together; beside it the letter lock of six slots

marks.same: the letter lock from the earlier example is set beside the locker
marks.slot: one slot of the locker turns through the letters and then the digits

narration: <bookmark mark='same'/>We solve this the same way as the example in your book.
<bookmark mark='slot'/>Count the choices for one slot first. Then multiply, once for each slot.

beats.on_screen: Given: 5 slots; each slot is one of 26 letters or 10 digits

marks.given: five slots are drawn, each marked 26 letters or 10 digits

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, a passcode with five slots. Each slot holds one of twenty six letters or ten digits.

beats.on_screen: To find: the number of passcodes

marks.find: the words number of passcodes are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find how many passcodes are possible.

marks.letters: 26 letters are shown beside one slot
marks.digits: 10 digits are shown beside the letters

narration: <bookmark mark='letters'/>Step one, count the choices for one slot. There are twenty six letters.
<bookmark mark='digits'/>There are also ten digits, and a slot takes only one of them.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>Twenty six plus ten gives thirty six choices for each slot.

beats.on_screen: 36 x 36 x 36 x 36 x 36 = 36^5, one 36 for each slot

marks.each: a 36 is written under each of the five slots

narration: <bookmark mark='each'/>Step two, multiply the choices of the five slots, because every choice goes with all the others.
<bookmark mark='power'/>That is thirty six multiplied five times, which is thirty six to the power five.

marks.five: 1679616 x 36 is written, the result is left blank

narration: <bookmark mark='two'/>Step three, multiply one slot at a time. Thirty six times thirty six gives one thousand two hundred and ninety six.
<bookmark mark='three'/>Times thirty six again gives forty six thousand six hundred and fifty six.
<bookmark mark='four'/>Times thirty six once more gives sixteen lakh seventy nine thousand six hundred and sixteen.
<bookmark mark='five'/>The last slot multiplies that by thirty six.

beats.on_screen: check: the last digit of each result is 6, because 6 x 6 = 36 ends in 6

marks.check: the last digits 6, 6, 6 are circled in the results so far

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step four, check the last digit. Each result so far ends in six.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>Six times six ends in six, so the final result must end in six too.

marks.num: 36^5 = 60466176 appears with its last digit 6 circled

narration: <bookmark mark='pay'/>Five slots of thirty six choices make thirty six to the power five passcodes.
<bookmark mark='num'/>That is six crore four lakh sixty six thousand one hundred and seventy six codes. It ends in six.
